jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]きます。
en: My mother gets up at six every morning.
why: A clock time you can point to takes に; を cannot mark a time.

jp: 父[ちち]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]七時[しちじ]半[はん]{に|ni-time}家[いえ]{を/から|o-departure}出[で]ます。
en: My father leaves the house at seven thirty every morning.
why: 出る takes the place you leave as its object, so 家 is marked with を.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}駅[えき]{で|de-place}電車[でんしゃ]{に|ni-target}乗[の]ります。
en: My little brother gets on the train at the station.
why: 乗る takes the vehicle you board with に, never を.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は/が|wa-topic}次[つぎ]{の|no-possessive}駅[えき]{で|de-place}電車[でんしゃ]{を/から|o-departure}降[お]ります。
en: My younger sister gets off the train at the next station.
why: 降りる names the vehicle you leave with を (or から); に is for boarding with 乗る.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{は/が|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]近[ちか]く{の|no-possessive}公園[こうえん]{を/で|o-path}散歩[さんぽ]します。
en: My grandmother takes a walk through the nearby park every day.
why: The area you walk through when taking a stroll is marked with を.

jp: 娘[むすめ]{は/が|wa-topic}五時[ごじ]{に|ni-time}家[いえ]{に/へ|ni-destination}帰[かえ]ります。
en: My daughter comes home at five.
why: 帰る aims at a destination, so the place you return to takes に.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}毎晩[まいばん]お風呂[ふろ]{に|ni-target}入[はい]ります。
en: I take a bath every evening.
why: 入る takes the thing you enter with に, so お風呂 is marked with に.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}ノック{を|o-object}しないで部屋[へや]{に|ni-target}入[はい]ります。
en: My little brother goes into the room without knocking.
why: 入る takes the room you enter with に; を would be for leaving it (出る).

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}朝[あさ]六時[ろくじ]{に|ni-time}部屋[へや]{の|no-possessive}カーテン{を|o-object}開[あ]けます。
en: My mother opens the curtains in the room at six in the morning.
why: The curtains are what gets opened, so they are the direct object and take を.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}夜[よる]十一時[じゅういちじ]{に|ni-time}電気[でんき]{を|o-object}消[け]します。
en: I turn off the light at eleven at night.
why: The light is the thing being switched off, so it is the direct object with を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}庭[にわ]{で/に|de-place}洗濯物[せんたくもの]{を|o-object}干[ほ]します。
en: My mother hangs the laundry out in the garden.
why: The laundry is what is being hung up, so it is the direct object with を.

jp: 父[ちち]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]犬[いぬ]{を|o-object}散歩[さんぽ]{に|ni-purpose}連[つ]れて行[い]きます。
en: My father takes the dog for a walk every morning.
why: The dog is what is taken along, so it is the object; に marks the walk as the purpose.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}犬[いぬ]{に|ni-recipient}毎朝[まいあさ]水[みず]{を|o-object}やります。
en: I give the dog water every morning.
why: The dog receives the water, so the recipient takes に and the water takes を.

jp: 姉[あね]{は/が|wa-topic}猫[ねこ]{に|ni-recipient}ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}あげました。
en: My older sister fed the cat.
why: The food is the thing given, so it is the direct object; に is already used for the cat.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]祖母[そぼ]{に|ni-target}電話[でんわ]{を|o-object}かけます。
en: My mother phones my grandmother every morning.
why: 電話をかける aims the call at a person, and that person takes に.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]、私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}祖母[そぼ]{に/と|ni-target}会[あ]います。
en: On Sundays I meet my grandmother.
why: 会う takes the person you meet with に (or と), never を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}弟[おとうと]{を|o-object}七時[しちじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]こします。
en: My mother wakes my little brother at seven.
why: 起こす is transitive: the person being woken is the direct object, marked with を.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は/が|wa-topic}ソファ{に|ni-target}座[すわ]ります。
en: My younger sister sits on the sofa.
why: 座る takes the seat you sit on with に, not を.

jp: 祖父[そふ]{は/が|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]ラジオ{を|o-object}聞[き]きます。
en: My grandfather listens to the radio every day.
why: The radio programme is what is listened to, so it is the direct object with を.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{は/が|wa-topic}孫[まご]{に|ni-recipient}毎月[まいつき]お小遣[こづか]い{を|o-object}あげます。
en: My grandmother gives her grandchild pocket money every month.
why: The grandchild is the person who receives the money, so the recipient takes に.

jp: 父[ちち]{は/が|wa-topic}庭[にわ]{の|no-possessive}花[はな]{に|ni-recipient}水[みず]{を|o-object}やります。
en: My father waters the flowers in the garden.
why: 水をやる gives water to something, and the thing that receives it takes に.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]歯[は]{を|o-object}磨[みが]きます。
en: I brush my teeth every morning.
why: The teeth are what you brush, so they are the direct object with を.

jp: 姉[あね]{は/が|wa-topic}朝[あさ]、シャワー{を|o-object}浴[あ]びます。
en: My older sister takes a shower in the morning.
why: 浴びる takes what you bathe in as its object, so シャワー takes を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}毎晩[まいばん]お皿[さら]{を|o-object}洗[あら]います。
en: My mother washes the dishes every evening.
why: The dishes are what get washed, so they are the direct object with を.

jp: 父[ちち]{は/が|wa-topic}土曜日[どようび]{に|ni-time}車[くるま]{を|o-object}洗[あら]います。
en: My father washes the car on Saturdays.
why: The car is what gets washed, so it is the direct object with を; に already marks the day.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は/が|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]ピアノ{を|o-object}練習[れんしゅう]します。
en: My younger sister practises the piano every day.
why: What you practise is the direct object of 練習する, so it takes を.

jp: 兄[あに]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]小[ちい]さい橋[はし]{を|o-path}渡[わた]ります。
en: My older brother crosses a small bridge every morning.
why: 渡る takes the thing you cross as a path, and that path is marked with を.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}家[いえ]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{の|no-possessive}道[みち]{を|o-path}まっすぐ歩[ある]きます。
en: I walk straight along the road in front of my house.
why: The road you move along while walking is a path, and a path takes を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]スーパー{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{を|o-path}通[とお]ります。
en: My mother passes in front of the supermarket every day.
why: 通る takes the place you pass by or through as a path, marked with を.

jp: 娘[むすめ]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]八時[はちじ]{に|ni-time}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: My daughter goes to school at eight every morning.
why: 行く heads for a destination, and the place you go to takes に (or へ).

jp: 家族[かぞく]{は/が|wa-topic}日曜日[にちようび]{に|ni-time}スーパー{に/へ|ni-destination}買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます。
en: On Sundays the family goes shopping at the supermarket.
why: The purpose of going is marked with に after a noun like 買い物.

jp: 父[ちち]{は/が|wa-topic}朝[あさ]、コーヒー{を|o-object}飲[の]みます。
en: My father drinks coffee in the morning.
why: The coffee is what gets drunk, so it is the direct object with を.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]パン{を|o-object}食[た]べます。
en: I eat bread every morning.
why: The bread is what gets eaten, so it is the direct object with を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}夜[よる]十時[じゅうじ]{に|ni-time}窓[まど]{を|o-object}閉[し]めます。
en: My mother closes the windows at ten at night.
why: The windows are what gets closed, so they are the direct object with を.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}犬[いぬ]{は/が|wa-topic}いつも玄関[げんかん]{に|ni-location}います。
en: Our dog is always at the front door.
why: いる says where someone or something is, and that place takes に.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}今[いま]、自分[じぶん]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{に|ni-location}います。
en: My little brother is in his own room now.
why: With いる, the place where someone is takes に.

jp: 祖父母[そふぼ]{は/が|wa-topic}大阪[おおさか]{に|ni-location}住[す]んでいます。
en: My grandparents live in Osaka.
why: 住む takes the place where you live with に, not を.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]、母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}ゴミ{を|o-object}出[だ]します。
en: Every morning my mother puts out the rubbish.
why: 出す is transitive: the rubbish is what gets put out, so it takes を.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}八時[はちじ]{に|ni-time}玄関[げんかん]{を/から|o-departure}出[で]ます。
en: My little brother goes out through the front door at eight.
why: 出る marks the place you leave with を, never に.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}誰[だれ]{を|o-object}待[ま]っています{か|ka-question}。
en: Who is my mother waiting for?
why: 待つ takes the person you wait for as its object, so 誰 takes を.

jp: 娘[むすめ]さん{は|wa-topic}新[あたら]しい学校[がっこう]{に|ni-target}もう慣[な]れました{か|ka-question}。
en: Has your daughter got used to her new school yet?
why: 慣れる takes the thing you get used to with に; it never takes a direct object with を.

jp: 兄[あに]{は/が|wa-topic}朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}食[た]べないで、会社[かいしゃ]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きました。
en: My older brother went to the office without eating breakfast.
why: The office is where he went to, so the destination takes に (or へ).

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}部屋[へや]{の|no-possessive}電気[でんき]{を|o-object}消[け]さないで寝[ね]ました。
en: My little brother went to sleep without turning off the light in his room.
why: The light is what is not switched off, so it is the direct object with を.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{が/は|ga-subject}家[いえ]{に/へ|ni-destination}来[き]ました。
en: A friend came to my house.
why: 来る moves toward a destination, so the place arrived at takes に (or へ).

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{が/は|ga-subject}遊[あそ]び{に|ni-purpose}来[き]ました。
en: My grandmother came to visit.
why: The purpose of coming is marked with に after a verb stem like 遊び.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}赤[あか]ちゃん{を|o-object}ベッド{に/で|ni-destination}寝[ね]かせました。
en: My mother put the baby to bed.
why: The bed is where the baby ends up, so that place takes に; the baby is the object.

jp: 姉[あね]{は/が|wa-topic}毎晩[まいばん]子[こ]ども{に|ni-recipient}絵本[えほん]{を|o-object}読[よ]んであげます。
en: My older sister reads picture books to her child every night.
why: The child is the one who is read to, so the recipient takes に and the book takes を.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{は/が|wa-topic}孫[まご]{を|o-object}いつもほめます。
en: My grandmother always praises her grandchildren.
why: ほめる takes the person praised as its direct object, so 孫 takes を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}玄関[げんかん]{で|de-place}お客[きゃく]さん{を|o-object}迎[むか]えました。
en: My mother welcomed the guest at the front door.
why: 迎える takes the person you welcome as its direct object, marked with を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}私[わたし]{に|ni-target}「早[はや]く寝[ね]なさい」{と|to-quote}言[い]いました。
en: My mother told me to go to bed early.
why: 言う takes the person addressed with に, while the words themselves are quoted with と.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{は/が|wa-topic}私[わたし]{を|o-object}家[いえ]{に/へ|ni-destination}呼[よ]びました。
en: My friend invited me to their house.
why: 呼ぶ takes the person you invite as its direct object; the house is the destination.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]、私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}母[はは]{を|o-object}手伝[てつだ]います。
en: Every evening I help my mother.
why: 手伝う takes the person you help as its direct object, marked with を.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は/が|wa-topic}玄関[げんかん]{で|de-place}靴[くつ]{を|o-object}脱[ぬ]ぎます。
en: My little brother takes off his shoes at the front door.
why: The shoes are what gets taken off, so they are the direct object with を.

jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]新聞[しんぶん]{を|o-object}ポスト{から|kara-from}取[と]ります。
en: My mother takes the newspaper from the mailbox every morning.
why: The newspaper is what gets taken, so it is the direct object with を.

jp: 夜[よる]、祖父[そふ]{は/が|wa-topic}テレビ{を|o-object}見[み]ます。
en: In the evening my grandfather watches television.
why: The television programme is what gets watched, so it is the direct object with を.
